segments: Understand the boundaries and working relationships between Wine, Proton, and Bottles so you can choose appropriately for each use case.
Technical lineage: the full evolutionary picture
Key points:

Wine is one of the upstream projects behind the core compatibility engine. Proton also integrates DXVK, VKD3D-Proton, runtimes, media components, and other projects; not every line of Proton code can be traced back to Wine. Some improvements can return upstream, but this needs to be checked against individual commits.

Proton is a Wine integration and patch collection aimed at the Steam gaming ecosystem, including a dedicated runtime environment. Non-game applications may work, but they are not its main support target. Proton patches may introduce compatibility bugs in non-game applications.

Proton-GE/CachyOS are different community-maintained builds and patch combinations. Their DXVK/VKD3D components, hardware adaptations, and game fixes depend on the specific release. They cannot bypass game anti-cheat policies and are not designed for reliably running Office or Photoshop.
Bottles and Lutris are managers. They do not translate APIs; they wrap command-line interfaces.
The three-layer model of engines and managers
Analogy
Role
Metaphor
A general-purpose engine: powers many kinds of vehicle, but needs tuning
A racing engine: designed for speed (frame rate), but may be less suitable elsewhere
A complete car: the engine is installed, with a steering wheel and dashboard ready to use

Decision flowchart
Principle
Use Proton for games and its ecosystem, Wine for general-purpose applications, and Bottles for efficient management.
Comparing versions and support scope
Do not group stable releases, development releases, community rolling builds, and manager names in a single “latest stable version” column. When recording versions, check each separately:
Component
Identity to record
Capabilities you cannot infer from the name alone
Release or development version, distribution package build, patches, and architecture
Whether the new WoW64, NTSYNC, and Wayland are actually available in that build
Official Proton
The exact version and runtime selected in Steam
Whether the current game, GPU, media functionality, and anti-cheat are supported
Official release, verification sources, and downloaded additional DLLs
Whether upscaling, frame generation, and specific game fixes work; whether umu is used outside Steam
Name, component manifest, and specific version
The current defaults such as Soda/Caffe, underlying Wine version, and patch scope
Versions actually bundled with the runner, and driver requirements
Vulkan features, ray tracing, performance, and multi-GPU paths

The 2025–2026 comparison table in the source material lacked sufficient release evidence to support its “latest” claims. Access to the WineHQ release page was restricted during this review, so the specific status of Wine 11.x is not confirmed. Checks of the official Proton and GE READMEs also reflect only the project documentation available at the time of access; read the release notes for any older release you select.

Version updates may modify prefixes or download new components. Keep a runner you can revert to and back up prefixes while they are not running. Test with the same application scenario; a single successful run does not establish long-term stability or security support.
